claims.statement: The harness's gate verifiability doctrine requires every gate to enforce exactly one evidence tier — traceability (structure matches), provenance (evidence re-derived from the source of truth), or truth (behavior re-run) — and to document `Verifies:` and `Does not verify:` lines.

SUMMARY.md's `### Not auto-verified` section states the change's negative scope: claims no gate checks, each labelled with the tier it reached; an unlisted unverified claim is the defect, and `- none` is only valid when every claim has a Verify row.

The SUMMARY `### Intent` section holds the user's request verbatim (or an `Intent-source:` pin to intent.md) and serves as the plan-blind oracle for intent-review, kept out of PLAN.md so the intent oracle stays independent of the plan oracle.

The SUMMARY header block (Lane, Confidence, Reason, Flags, Affects, Input-type) is machine-read: commit-gate.sh corroborates `Lane:` against the staged diff and the trust-metrics ledger reads Lane/Confidence/Flags.

`scripts/verify_summary.py --lane` is the single source of truth for the lane-to-evidence mapping: tiny requires filled Lane/Confidence/Reason, normal adds a non-placeholder `### Verify` row, and high-risk adds a real `### Rollback` (the untouched `git revert <sha>` template line is rejected).
Lane mode never executes Verify commands; it is a traceability check, and its warn-only advisories are printed on passing as well as failing runs.

The high-risk `### Not auto-verified` requirement is warn-only by default and becomes blocking when REQUIRE_NOT_AUTO_VERIFIED is set to a value other than empty/0/false; it accepts `- none` and rejects a missing section, comment-only content, or the unedited template bullet, without verifying completeness or tier correctness.

For a SUMMARY whose Input-type starts with bug fix/bug-fix/bugfix, the lane check requires a `red` row running `scripts/run_at_commit.py <7-40 hex sha> -- <test>` with claimed exit 1-123 and a `green` row with the same normalized test command and claimed exit 0, or a `Red test exempt: <reason>` line; this is advisory unless REQUIRE_RED_TEST=1.

When the sibling PLAN.md declares an SC table, every valid SC-n must be named in a Verify row's Criterion column with a claimed exit matching the SC's expected exit, and an unknown Criterion id is an error; with no PLAN or no SC table the coverage check fails open. SC coverage errors fail both lane mode and `--check` mode.
PLAN.md SC `Expected` cells must lead with the machine-read token `exit <n>`; duplicates or malformed Expected cells are reported as SC table errors, and SC tables inside code fences are ignored.

Verify mode re-runs each non-placeholder Verify command via shell at the repo root with a per-command timeout (default 60s, timeout reported as exit 124); a row passes when actual exit equals the claimed exit (non-zero claims are valid negative proof) and fails on mismatch, unclaimed non-zero exit, timeout, or an actual exit that differs from its Criterion SC's expected exit.
Trivial commands (`true`, `:`, `exit 0`, bare `echo`) are rejected as non-evidence without being executed; the denylist is best-effort and wrapped no-ops are not caught.

Without `--check`, verify_summary.py rewrites the Exit column with actual exit codes in row order and writes a `Verified:` timestamp only when every row passed, dropping any existing stamp on failure; `--check` compares without modifying the file.

`verify_summary.py --sc-history <slug> --base <ref>` is a provenance check over git history: it flags an SC that a branch commit recorded as failing (judged only where the Verify row is new or changed) and whose Check/Expected later changed or whose row was removed at HEAD, unless HEAD's `### Deviations` names it; it exits 0 on findings unless REQUIRE_SC_STABLE=1.

The optional SUMMARY runtime metadata check is format-only: `Runtime-mode` and `Runtime-evidence-id` must be absent or supplied together, with mode in enforced/advisory/unsupported and id matching `codex-mode-<16 hex>`; it never compares against the local .harness-state record.

commit-gate.sh check_lane_evidence materializes the staged (index) SUMMARY.md and PLAN.md into a temp directory and runs `verify_summary.py --lane <tmp> --plan-dir <tmpdir>`, so the committed tree is judged and a commit that records the evidence self-unblocks; it fails open when python3 or the script is unavailable.
Under REQUIRE_VERIFY=1 app gates, commit-gate.sh requires a `### Verify` block when app/ files are staged and re-runs it with `verify_summary.py --check <slug>`, blocking on mismatch.

ci-strict-gate.sh blocks a PR touching hooks/, settings.json, templates/ or render_plan.py unless a changed `Lane: high-risk` SUMMARY with a real Verify row passes `verify_summary.py --check`; scripts/ changes (excluding scripts/test_*) get the same check warn-only unless REQUIRE_SCRIPTS_PROOF=1, and the gate does not verify that the rows cover the change.

ci-strict-gate.sh runs `verify_summary.py --sc-history` for every slug whose PLAN.md or SUMMARY.md changed in the PR, before the gated-path tier selection, and under REQUIRE_SC_STABLE=1 blocks on findings, check errors, or a renamed spec directory.

check_verify_rows.py lints changed SUMMARY Verify rows and PLAN SC Check cells to be pipe-free (quoted `|` allowed) and not full-suite/build commands that would exceed the 60s strict-gate cap; run-tests.sh feeds it only SUMMARY/PLAN files changed vs base and since a grandfather cutoff commit.

run_at_commit.py runs a command in a temporary detached git worktree at a given commit and returns the command's exit code, 128+n on signal, 124 on its 50-second timeout, or 125 on a helper failure, removing the worktree afterwards.

check_review_receipt.py validates specs/<slug>/.review-receipt.json: reviewed_head_sha must be a full 40-hex sha equal to HEAD, or differ only by changes under specs/; every recorded review must have result `pass` and integer blocking_open of 0; and each `--require` type must be present with pass.

With `--require-audit-if <base>`, check_review_receipt.py adds `context-propagation-audit` to the required review types when base..HEAD touches a workflow-engine surface (skills SKILL.md/prompt files, agents/*.md, rules/*.md, excluding README and templates), using a regex kept byte-identical to commit-gate.sh, and fails closed when the base cannot be diffed.

finishing-a-development-branch runs `check_review_receipt.py <plan_dir> --require correctness,intent --require-audit-if <base>` for non-tiny work before push, and a missing, stale, failing or blocking receipt stops the flow.

ESCALATIONS.md is a deny-on-no-response channel for blocking decisions (commit-gate denies commits touching the slug while any decision is pending), whereas QUESTIONS.md holds only non-blocking open questions checked by check_open_questions.py when their closes-at slug ships, warn-first unless REQUIRE_QUESTIONS_CLOSED=1.
An intent.md copied from INTENT.template.md gates intake: intake proceeds only when its Status header is approved, and committing it with Status approved constitutes the approval.

For each matched red/green pair in a bug-fix SUMMARY, lane mode's fix-diff check requires at least one path that differs between the red commit and the index outside `specs/` and outside the paths the red commit itself changed (via `git diff-tree`); otherwise it reports `bug fix: no code change after red commit <sha> outside specs/ and the red test files`. The red command's tokens are not used.

The fix-diff check runs under the same REQUIRE_RED_TEST switch as the red/green check: both lane callers invoke `_red_fix_diff_issue` beside `_red_green_issue`, so its findings are `!` advisories by default and exit-1 errors when the switch is set.

When git is missing, the cwd is not in a git repository, or the red sha does not resolve, the fix-diff check reports `bug fix: cannot check the fix diff for red commit <sha> -- <cause>` instead of passing (an unverifiable claim is not a pass).

The fix-diff check resolves the repository from the process cwd (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and compares against the index (`git diff --cached`), so it works on the commit gate's temp copy of the SUMMARY and counts a staged-but-uncommitted fix but not an unstaged edit.
The fix-diff check only considers red rows with a matching green row and makes no git call for a non-bug-fix SUMMARY or one carrying a `Red test exempt:` line with a non-empty reason.

The fix-diff check is provenance-tier: it proves that something changed after the red commit, not that the change fixes the bug or that the red exit was real; because it diffs to the current index, later commits make an old bug-fix SUMMARY pass.
